batches.objective: Select one Vulkan generated-program optimization from recoverable unchanged-application execution cost.
batches.rationale: The retained loop-invariant candidate produces fewer instructions but lacks the declared GPU gain and repeatedly regresses complete-operation medians. UMAP pass times account for only part of ordinary operation cost. Select the next correction from measured application contribution. Subgroup normalization removes the VGPR discrepancy; width 64 fails the shader-gain requirement and supplies no repeatable ordinary benefit. Do not interpret reported register count as recoverable lowering cost.
batches.nextAction: Identify a recoverable cost in unchanged UMAP SGD execution with subgroup width and execution conditions matched, using final instructions and actual pass timing. Do not revive rejected hoisting or width 64; select one general IR/SPIR-V improvement only after measuring application contribution.
acceptance: Numerical, bounds and alias semantics are preserved through independent physical output oracles; existing runtime and full WGSL suites pass.

Compiler time and allocations, generated-program execution time, full application latency and memory are measured independently against the accepted baseline and pinned Dawn, with declared regression limits and every cohort retained.
batches.stopCondition: Retain or reject one measured Vulkan candidate; no shader optimization or application superiority is inferred from preparation savings alone.
requiredEnvironment: Physical AMD Vulkan provider and final-program profiling
Pinned Dawn control and unchanged application inputs
